messages:
support-ryan: FYI customer acct acct-9876 reporting sudden 429 spikes and huge tail latency. They see requests routed to APAC from EU clients which adds ~600ms. Also intermittent 401s. Customer repro steps included.

sre-jen: Can you paste the exact example call + headers they used? Also need first/last request IDs or x-request-id if available.

support-ryan: Pasting what customer sent: 
```
POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer <token-redacted>
Region: eu-west1
Body: {"prompt":"..."}
```
They show response headers: `x-region-served: apac1`, `x-rate-limit-remaining: 0`, and `x-request-id: req_0a1b2c`.

opsbot (incident-bot): Incident created INC-2026-0427-44 for cross-region failover & auth retry loop (assigned: sre).

devon: I rolled out the new geo-routing policy (prefer-capacity) ~2h before the first report. It prefers regions with available burst even if not affinity-safe. Could be overshooting capacity advertisements for eu nodes.

infra-alex: Looking at control plane advert logs — eu cluster advertised 0 available extra slots for GPU-pool-eu-2 between 2026-04-27T08:10 and 08:32 UTC. That would cause fanout to next region (apac). snippet: 
```
[08:12:01] pool-eu-2 capacity=2 reserved=2 available=0
[08:13:04] pool-eu-2 heartbeat missed
```

maria: Customer also ran a long-run loop to repro. Steps they gave: 1) issue 20 parallel requests with same token; 2) after ~10 requests they see alternating 429 / 401; 3) later requests show served-by apac1. Example curl they used: 
```
for i in {1..20}; do curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -X POST \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n  -H "Region: eu-west1" \n  -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &\ndone
```

sre-jen: Alternating 429/401 suggests token rate-limits + auth validation hitting different control planes. When requests cross region we sometimes hit a cached token TTL mismatch on the downstream region causing transient 401 until cache refresh. Need to confirm if auth cache TTL was recently changed.

billing-bot: Alert: Unusually high token billing for acct-9876 between 2026-04-27T08:00-09:00 UTC. Estimated delta +480%.

devon: Confirmed — we shipped a small optimization that reduced auth cache TTL from 60s -> 10s in the hopes of faster revocations. That could produce bursts of auth validation traffic across regions. We should revert for EU until we patch routing.

infra-alex: Short repro from our side: sent 50 concurrent requests with same token and saw: 
```
200 x10 (eu), 429 x15 (eu overflow), 401 x8 (apac auth-miss), 200 x17 (apac)
```
Also observed `x-region-served` flip after eu pool reported available=0.

product-lina: Customer impact is high. We need a mitigation path: 1) temporarily pin requests from this customer to eu via tenant affinity; 2) increase per-tenant burst quota for them (manual override) so they don't get 429 while we fix routing; 3) revert auth TTL change.

sre-jen: Agreed. Proposed immediate actions: 
- infra-alex: run `rlctl tenant set-affinity acct-9876 eu` (will keep them on EU nodes) 
- devon: rollback auth-ttl change (PR already flagged) 
- support-ryan: notify customer of temporary mitigation and ask for request IDs if they still see 401s after pinning

infra-alex: Running affinity pin now, will post completion.

opsbot (incident-bot): INC-2026-0427-44 updated: mitigation applied (tenant affinity pin), assigned to devon for auth TTL rollback.

devon: Rolling back auth-ttl now, patching will take ~5m to rollout across auth-proxies.

support-ryan: I'll email the customer with the steps we applied and ask them to retest using the same loop. Will paste their response here.

sre-jen: After mitigation let's follow up with a postmortem: root cause appears to be interplay between reduced auth cache TTL + prefer-capacity routing causing cross-region fanout when eu advertises zero capacity. Action items: add circuit-breaker to avoid auth validation flood across regions, and add a per-tenant soft-affinity threshold to avoid immediate fanout for small capacity blips.

maria: Customer confirmed reduced 401s/429s after pinning and rollback — latency back to normal. They sent logs showing `x-region-served: eu-west1` consistently. :relieved:

support-ryan: Closing loop with them and keeping incident open for postmortem. Thanks all :thumbsup:
